analysis.title: Market reactions and central bank announcements
key_insights: US equities rose about 1.5% after the midterm elections, in line with gains in European and Swedish stocks. Markets read the result as less scope for major new fiscal spending and lower geopolitical risk.
Oil fell to USD 94 per barrel, the US 10-year Treasury yield declined about 5 basis points and the dollar weakened across the board after the midterms.

The rotation out of AI was two-sided. Companies directly exposed to data centre expansion fell, while the tech giants rose because they are now expected to scale back investment, which improves cash flows.
Euro area inflation rose to 4.0% on energy. Core inflation held at 2.5%, broadly sideways for several months and in line with ECB forecasts.

Euro area services inflation rose 0.1 percentage points on base effects. Food prices rose for both processed and unprocessed food, which could be an early sign that higher energy prices and possibly drought are feeding into other prices.
SEB expects the ECB to hike in December, driven more by the balance of risks than by the latest inflation figures.

SEB and the market expect a 25bp Bank of England hike to 4.00%. SEB sees it as an insurance move rather than the start of a new tightening cycle, and considers market pricing of around four further hikes excessive. A follow-up hike in February is possible.
Norges Bank is expected to hold at 4.50%. SEB thinks rates have already peaked, while markets see roughly equal odds of a hike and a hold in December.

The Riksbank raised its rate to 2.00%, its first hike in three years. The press release was more dovish and the press conference more hawkish. SEB forecasts further hikes in February and May, but the risk is that they come later or are fewer.

Swedish CPIF is expected at +0.3% m/m with the annual rate slowing to 1.4%. CPIF excluding energy is expected at 0.4% y/y, 0.2 percentage points below the Riksbank's forecast. SEB expects inflation to rise in a few months as electricity costs and the restored fuel tax take effect.

sector_views.rationale: Midterm outcome split the AI trade. Data centre-exposed names fell, while the large tech companies gained on expected lower investment and better cash flows.
